sections.title: Writing: A letter to the editor
sections.instructions: Identify the article, express your opinion, support it with at least two details in your own words, consider another view, and conclude with a suggestion. Use a formal tone and at least three hedging expressions.

questions.prompt: Write your own 200–250 word letter to the editor responding to the article.

sections.passage:
Start: Dear Editor,
Paragraph 1: article and opinion.
Paragraphs 2–3: reasons, article evidence and another viewpoint.
Paragraph 4: conclusion or suggestion.
Close: Yours faithfully, + your name.
Useful phrases: I am writing in response to…; While I recognise…; I am not entirely convinced…; Furthermore…; Nevertheless…; I would therefore argue…
Hedging: believe, suggest, appear, seem, may, might, could, would, perhaps, probably, somewhat, to some extent.
Rubric: response/opinion 2; evidence/reasons 2; organisation/format 2; vocabulary/tone/hedging 2; grammar/spelling/punctuation 2.
